Adventure story chooser: historical entity introduction, native source grammar

Source images are the offline PE files configured by data/runtime/native-pe-images.json:
  reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
  classic   PE:6a70b91c:0270a000
Actual C output is produced by Ghidra 12.1.4. The accompanying .asm files retain
original native instructions, and the TSVs retain call operands, literal
addresses, conditional branches and actual indexed jump destinations. These
are extracted source material, not game observations or regression artifacts.

Entry and display consumer
  reference chooser 0x870260; classic 0x86dae0.
  The entity branch initializes a native history context with all focus IDs -1,
  copies the selected option's +0x68 entity ID to context +0x1c, and calls
  history::describe(global history, context, brief=true, output string).
  reference call 0x8712c8; consumer 0x8712e4 -> 0x858550.
  Output begins with [C:6:0:1]. history::describe builds the introduction,
  confidence paragraph, and [B], then returns before the event/relation loops
  because brief=true. The complete nonbrief function is retained as source,
  including its other focus types, military history and relationship prose.
  reference history::describe 0xb8eeb0..0xb9241c (native extent 0xb92634).
  classic   history::describe 0xb8bef0..0xb8f45c (native extent 0xb8f674).

Entity introduction, in native output order
  1. Entity-name helper, then literal " was a".
     If entity flags +0x9c bit 0x400 is clear, append " " and singular species
     using entity +0x98 WORD, r9b=1, caste=-1, plural=false.
     Invalid race IDs produce "creature"; otherwise RAW adjective selection
     uses caste-specific +0x60 with fallback to creature RAW +0x60.
  2. Entity type +0 WORD:
       0:  " civilization of "
       5:  " religion of "
       4:  " bandit gang from "
       6:  " " + military adjective + " " + military noun + " from "
       8:  " performance troupe from "
       7:  " collection of outcasts from "
       9:  " merchant company from "
      10:  " " + guild profession + " guild from "
      all other values: " group from "
  3. World language-name formatter, mode 2.
  4. Military religion and specialization clauses, or religion deity/force
     clauses, as below.
  5. ".  " + knowledge confidence paragraph + "[B]".

Military adjective and noun, type 6
  entity +0xd30 <= 10: "mercenary".
  Otherwise +0xd6c > 10: "versatile mercenary".
  Otherwise: "shadowy military".
  Nonempty pointer vector +0x1330..+0x1338: "order".
  Otherwise +0xd6c <= 10: "band"; otherwise "company".

Military religious clause
  Require entity flags +0x9c bit 0x2000000 and nonempty deity ID vector
  +0xfc8..+0xfd0 (DWORD elements).
  Scan entity-link pointer vector +0xb8..+0xc0 from the beginning. A link
  type +0 WORD == 2 whose +4 entity ID resolves to entity type 5 supplies
  " linked to " plus that religion's name, if its entity +4 ID is not -1.
  If no such usable religion supplies text:
    deity count > 1: " devoted to worship".
    deity count == 1: " devoted to the worship of " + historical figure name.
  Remember whether this clause was produced to prefix specialization by " and".

Military specialization
  Require weapon WORD vector +0x148..+0x150 length <= 3, nonempty skill WORD
  vector +0x1c50..+0x1c58, and (+0xd70 > 10 or +0xd40 > 10).
  +0xd70 > 10: " dedicated to the mastery of "; else " known for ".
  Empty weapon vector uses the first skill:
    99 "wrestling"; 100 "biting"; 101 "striking"; 102 "kicking".
    Other values add no skill token after the clause prefix.
  Nonempty weapon vector:
    if +0xd70 <= 10, prefix "their use of ".
    Each token is "the " + item_weapon RAW name at +0x68 (singular).
    Original separators are ", ", " and ", and ", and ".

Guild profession, type 10
  Scan pointer vector +0xa0..+0xa8 from the beginning for the first record
  with +0 DWORD == 0. Its +4 WORD is the profession ID.
  No such record or ID -1: "craft".
  Otherwise call native profession-title(out1, out2, profession,
  current-player-race WORD, &scratch, caste=-1, plural=true, capitalize=false),
  then append out1 only. This is a language RAW output boundary, not a
  civilization name, squad alias, or a text inferred from spelling.
  Native profession IDs 0..134 use the full switch retained in profession-title.c.
  profession 98/99 write "hunting"/"war" to out2 and keep out1 unchanged.
  profession 102 has no title assignment but follows the generic suffix path,
  therefore plural=true appends only the literal "s" to its initially empty out1.
  Other branches include irregular plural forms and child/baby RAW names.
  Profession 103 CHILD and 104 BABY, with no PROFESSION_NAME override and
  caste=-1: nonempty creature +0xc0/+0x80 singular names select creature
  +0xe0/+0xa0 plural names respectively; those selected plural names may be
  empty. Without a usable singular name the finite fallback is "children" or
  "babies". This differs from a helper rejecting an empty string.
  Custom PROFESSION_NAME availability and singular/plural selection are retained
  separately as profession-raw-title-available.c, profession-raw-title-selection.c
  and the latter's final creature selector profession-raw-creature-title.c.
  A permitted explicitly empty output remains empty. Do not replace a selected
  empty RAW plural by a guessed English fallback.

Religion clauses, type 5
  Deity count zero: no worship clause.
  Deity count > 1: " centered around the worship of various beings".
  Exactly one: resolve historical figure. A failed lookup adds no clause.
  A resolved figure adds " centered around the worship of " + figure name.
  Figure flag 2 (bit query at figure +0xc8) adds ", a ", optional RAW species
  for figure race +2/caste +4 when race != -1, a space, then sex +6:
    0 "goddess"; 1 "god"; all other values "deity".
  Nonempty deity sphere WORD vector adds " of " and all sphere names in
  reverse native order, separated by ", " and final " and ".
  sphere-name supplies the conditional "the " article and sphere-token supplies
  the complete 130-entry enum switch (0..129), both retained as actual C.
  Figure flag 3 adds ", a force" independently of flag 2.
  force-is-known scans world region pointer vector +0x238..+0x240 backward,
  finding the last region whose forces DWORD vector +0x250 contains figure
  +0xe0 ID. The lookup returns an optional index, accepted unless it is -1;
  this is a membership search, not a stored association value.
  No matching region: no region suffix.
  Found region: " which was said to permeate " in global game mode 3;
  otherwise " which permeates ", followed by region language-name mode 1.

Knowledge/confidence
  entity-historical-knowledge-tier counts history events whose virtual +0xc0
  predicate matches entity +4, event +0x18 is positive, and the first byte of
  event +0x10 data has mask 0x1 set. Tiers by count:
    0 -> 0, 1..4 -> 1, 5..9 -> 2, 10..49 -> 3, 50..99 -> 4, >=100 -> 5.
  knowledge-confidence-paragraph:
    0/other: no text.
    1: "A few issues still trouble scholars, but the picture is fairly clear.  "
    2: "Many facts are still unclear to historians.  "
    3: "It is still shrouded in mystery.  "
    4: "Its nature is still an intriguing puzzle to the learned.  "
    5: "Only the barest fragments of this amazing story have been uncovered.  It is one of the great untold tales of our times.  "

Unknown names and dynamic fields
  Entity-name helper uses entity +0x20 language-name, mode 1; flags bit 2 may
  add [LPAGE:ENT:id]...[/LPAGE]. Missing entity: "an unknown civilization".
  Historical-figure-name helper uses the supplied native history context,
  figure name, identity/speaker references, species and pronoun cases. Its
  full actual function is retained. Missing figure: "an unknown creature".
  Plain chooser entity context has zero speaker/identity payload pointers and
  all figure focus IDs -1, so the normal named figure path applies here.
  World/region/entity/figure names, adjective RAW strings, weapon RAW strings,
  and custom profession RAW strings are dynamic native data. Their complete
  finite formatting branches are in the C; the user's current generated names
  cannot be enumerated from the PE alone.
  No custom squad.alias is translated or reinterpreted by this source grammar.
